profile.campus: Northwest Omaha, Douglas County, Nebraska (Google's newer Omaha campus, announced 2022, 261 acres near State Street and Blair High Road)
profile.address: Rainwood Road, Union Precinct, Douglas County, Nebraska, 68142
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's northwest Omaha data center campus in Douglas County, announced in April 2022 as part of a $750 million Nebraska investment that year, itself part of a larger $9.5 billion national expansion Google announced across US data center and office sites. Google described the northwest Omaha project as a new multi-building campus on 261 acres near State Street and Blair High Road, planning roughly 1.4 million gross square feet across buildings up to four stories, and said that once operational the Omaha metro would hold the company's largest Google operational footprint of any US metro area, spanning this campus alongside the older Papillion site in neighboring Sarpy County and a newer Lincoln, Nebraska campus under construction on roughly 580 acres. Governor Pete Ricketts' administration said at the time it expected Google's Nebraska jobs to at least double with the new investment, covering technician, engineer, maintenance, and security roles at facilities that run 24 hours a day; Google separately pledged $100,000 toward Omaha's planned new main library. Since 2019 the company has created more than 120 jobs across its various Nebraska roles, and reports investing about $4.4 billion in the state cumulatively over the five years through 2024, including $930 million in 2024 alone. Google's own Nebraska data center location page does not identify which specific building on the northwest Omaha campus this OSM-mapped structure corresponds to, nor its individual square footage or MW capacity, so this registry records the 1.4-million-square-foot campus-wide figure as regional context rather than a fact specific to this building.

Omaha Public Power District, which serves the Douglas and Sarpy county campuses, has cited large-load data center demand from Google and other operators as a leading factor in its own long-range generation and transmission planning, and Nebraska's status as one of the few states where electricity is delivered entirely by public power districts rather than investor-owned utilities has repeatedly come up in coverage of why Google, Facebook, and other hyperscalers chose the Omaha-Lincoln corridor for a dense cluster of campuses.

reading.body:
This building sits on Google's northwest Omaha campus, a 261-acre multi-building project announced in 2022 as part of a $750 million Nebraska investment that year. Google has not published megawatt capacity for any individual building or the campus as a whole, so the size of this facility's computational footprint cannot be assessed from operator specifications. The campus is planned for roughly 1.4 million gross square feet across up to four stories, but no power budget or rack count is disclosed.

Google reports $4.4 billion in cumulative Nebraska infrastructure investment through 2024, including $930 million in 2024 alone, distributed across the Omaha metro, Lincoln, and the older Papillion site. The company has stated that once the northwest Omaha campus is fully operational, the Omaha metro will hold its largest operational presence of any US metropolitan area. Omaha Public Power District, which serves both the Douglas and Sarpy county campuses, has identified large-load data center demand from Google and other operators as a leading factor in its long-range generation and transmission planning.

Nebraska delivers electricity entirely through public power districts rather than investor-owned utilities, a factor that has been cited in coverage as a reason Google and other hyperscalers clustered campuses in the Omaha-Lincoln corridor. No capacity figure for this facility or campus is published by the operator, so its ranking among Nebraska's 21 mapped data center sites cannot be determined from disclosed specifications.
